options.why: Food is found in a habitat, but a habitat is a place.

options.text: the place where a living thing lives and finds what it needs

options.why: A baby animal is called its young, not a habitat.
Weather happens in a habitat, but a habitat is a place.

hints: Every living thing lives somewhere.
That place gives it food, water and shelter.
A pond, a forest and a desert are all examples.
items.explanation: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives. It gives the living thing food, water and shelter.

items.prompt: Match each animal to its habitat.
hints: Think about what each animal needs.
Which animal needs to keep its skin moist and lay eggs in water?
Which animal has thick fur for the cold?
items.explanation: Camels live in deserts and polar bears live in the Arctic. Frogs live in and around ponds, monkeys in rainforests and whales in the ocean.

items.prompt: How is a camel suited to living in the desert?

options.text: It has thick white fur to blend in with snow.
options.why: That describes a polar bear in the Arctic.

options.text: It has gills to breathe under water.
options.why: Fish have gills. Camels breathe air.

options.text: It can go a long time without drinking.
It has webbed feet for swimming.
options.why: Ducks and frogs have webbed feet. Camels have wide feet for sand.

hints: Deserts are hot and dry.
Water is hard to find in a desert.
What would help an animal where water is rare?
items.explanation: Deserts have very little water. Camels can go many days without drinking, and their wide feet stop them sinking into sand.

items.prompt: Many people think a camel's hump stores water. What does it really store?

options.why: This is a common mistake. The hump does not hold water.
The hump is not filled with air.
Sand does not get into a camel's hump.

hints: Think about how animals store energy for later.
The hump shrinks when a camel has not eaten for a long time.
Which store gives energy when food is scarce?
items.explanation: A camel's hump stores fat. The camel uses the fat for energy when food is hard to find.

items.prompt: Choose 2 ways a polar bear is suited to the cold Arctic.

options.text: a thick layer of fat under its skin

options.why: Big ears lose heat. Polar bears have small ears.
Polar bears need to keep warm, not cool.
Polar bears have no hump.

hints: The Arctic is very cold.
Look for features that keep heat in.
Cross out features for hot places.
items.explanation: A polar bear's thick fur and its layer of fat keep it warm. Its small ears also lose very little heat.

items.prompt: Mangrove trees grow in salty mud on Indonesian coasts. Some of their roots stick up out of the mud. Why?

options.text: to take in air, because the wet mud has very little

options.why: Trees do not eat fish. Plants make their own food.

options.text: to make the sea water fresh
options.why: The roots do not change the sea water.
Bees visit flowers, not roots.

hints: Roots need air as well as water.
Wet, muddy soil has very little air in it.
Where is there plenty of air?
items.explanation: Mangrove mud is wet and has little air. Roots that stick up into the air help the tree take in the air it needs.

items.prompt: Woodlice are often found under logs and stones. What conditions do they like?

options.why: Woodlice dry out quickly in bright, dry places.
Woodlice hide from the hot sun.
Woodlice prefer sheltered places.

hints: Think about what it is like under a log.
Is it light or dark under a stone?
Is the ground under a log wet or dry?
items.explanation: Under logs and stones it is dark and damp. Woodlice need damp places so their bodies do not dry out.

items.prompt: Sort the actions. Do they harm a habitat or help it?

items.text: picking up litter on a beach

hints: Think about the animals and plants that live there.
Does the action make their home cleaner or dirtier?
Start with planting trees.
items.explanation: Litter, cutting down forests and oil spills damage habitats. Planting trees, recycling and clearing litter help protect them.

items.prompt: Cactus plants grow well in deserts. Which feature helps a cactus save water?

options.why: Wide leaves lose lots of water. A cactus has spines instead.
Flowers do not help a cactus save water.

options.text: a thick stem that stores water

options.why: Desert soil is dry. Cactus roots spread wide to catch rain.

hints: Deserts get very little rain.
A cactus must keep the water it gets.
Which part could act like a water tank?
items.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick stem. Its spines lose much less water than wide leaves would.

items.prompt: Plastic rubbish in a river can harm fish and birds. Which action helps the river habitat most?

options.text: Pour soap into the river to clean it.
options.why: Soap pollutes the water too.

options.text: Catch all the fish and keep them at home.
options.why: This harms the river habitat even more.

options.text: Build a road along the river bank.
options.why: A road could add more pollution.

options.text: Put rubbish in bins and never in rivers.

hints: The problem is rubbish getting into the water.
Stop the problem where it starts.
Which action keeps rubbish out of the river?
items.explanation: Keeping rubbish out of rivers stops it harming fish and birds. Clean rivers are healthy habitats.

items.prompt: An animal has very large ears, pale sandy fur and furry feet. It hunts at night. Where does it most likely live?

options.why: Big ears lose heat. Arctic animals have small ears.
This animal has fur and feet for land.
Sandy fur and furry feet suit sand, not a pond.

hints: Large ears help an animal lose heat.
Sandy fur helps it hide.
Furry feet help on hot ground.
items.explanation: Large ears let out heat, and sandy fur hides it on sand. Furry feet protect it from hot sand, so it lives in a hot desert.

items.prompt: Choose an animal. Write how two of its features help it survive in its habitat.

criteria.label: Names an animal and its habitat
Describes two features of the animal
Explains how each feature helps it survive

items.model: A camel lives in the desert. It has wide, flat feet, so it does not sink into the sand. It can go for days without drinking because water is hard to find there.
hints: Think about what is hard about living in that habitat.
Use the word because to link each feature to its use.
items.explanation: A good answer links each feature to a problem in the habitat. For example, a polar bear's thick fur keeps it warm in the freezing Arctic.
